title: Coordinator RELEASE ignores DAOSequence; stale RELEASE drops a newer allocation
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness

ShortAddressCoordinator::process() uses last_sequence_by_eui only on the ALLOCATE path. The RELEASE path (around the `AssignmentOperation::Release` branch) deletes the live mapping for request.eui64 with no check against the stored DAOSequence.

Consequence: ALLOCATE seq=1, RELEASE seq=2 (ACK lost or delayed), ALLOCATE seq=3 (new mapping installed), then a retransmitted RELEASE seq=2 still succeeds and removes the seq=3 assignment. The ALLOCATE path treats equal sequence as idempotent retransmission; RELEASE treats every sequence as authoritative.

A stale or replayed RELEASE is therefore destructive after re-acquisition. The same inequality test on ALLOCATE treats any sequence != last as a fresh request, so a stale ALLOCATE with a different sequence also renews the lease rather than being ignored as older.

Fix: apply RFC 6550 wrapping freshness (same sequence = idempotent copy, newer = new request, older = ignore) to both ALLOCATE and RELEASE before mutating the table. Dual-impl note: python/src/lichen/link/address_assignment.py has the same RELEASE gap; spec/vectors only require duplicate RELEASE of the current mapping to be idempotent, not clobbering a newer allocation.
close_reason: ShortAddressCoordinator::process now applies RFC 6550 Section 7.2 DAOSequence freshness to ALLOCATE and RELEASE before mutating. Same/older/incomparable sequences are ignored; last sequence is retained after RELEASE so a retransmitted RELEASE cannot drop a newer allocation. Tests cover the seq=1/2/3 replay, lease non-renewal, and 255->0 wrap. cargo test -p lichen-rpl --features std --lib address_assignment:: (12 passed) and --test address_assignment_vectors (11 passed).
